llm.summary: This travel skill is not clearly malicious, but it needs Review because it can automatically install an unpinned global CLI and persist raw travel queries in a local log.

dimensions.detail: Networked travel queries are expected for real-time inventory, but automatic global software installation and local logging of user queries exceed what is safely scoped or clearly controlled.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact instructs `npm i -g @fly-ai/flyai-cli` and an unpinned moving-branch `npx skills add` path; the CLI installation is global, unpinned, and may occur automatically when `flyai` is missing.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions redefine the agent as a CLI executor, prohibit fallback answers, require re-execution if booking links or branding are absent, and make package installation part of the normal workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The global CLI persists after use, and `references/runbook.md` directs appending raw input and execution details to `.flyai-execution-log.json` without consent, redaction, retention limits, or file permission guidance.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The real-time group-tour and booking-link behavior is coherent with the stated Fliggy/flyai travel purpose, but the skill forces provider-controlled booking links and branding without URL validation, opt-out, or clear third-party link warnings.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you trust the flyai CLI publisher and are comfortable with a global npm install, outbound travel searches, third-party booking links, and local retention of query details. Prefer pinning versions, requiring explicit approval before installation, validating booking-link domains, and disabling or redacting execution logs before use.
llm.findings:
[P6] unexpected: Downgraded: the cited artifact text is an output-format section, not an instruction to reveal system prompts or hidden rules.
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted as supply-chain risk: the README includes a moving branch install path rather than an immutable reviewed source.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Accepted for automatic unpinned global npm installation and for persistent local logging without explicit user control or safeguards.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese search phrases appear consistent with the Fliggy/flyai travel inventory use case, though the locale limitation should be disclosed more clearly.
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted: the runbook stores raw user queries and command details, which may include sensitive itinerary or personal information.
[SDI-1] expected: Downgraded: flyai branding is consistent with the README and parent skill reference, though the relationship between Fliggy and flyai could be clearer.
[T01] expected: Partially accepted as a scoping concern rather than malicious hijacking: using the CLI and booking links fits the skill, but mandatory branded booking links and no URL validation are over-prescriptive.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact directs installation and execution of an unpinned global npm CLI and documents an unpinned repository install path.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: the documented log persistence pattern stores raw input and uses shell interpolation that would be unsafe if followed literally.
